Phrasal Verbs and Useful Expressions

Letter        Expression                           Example Sentence

   A        admitted to        The patient was admitted to our hospital in March 2008 for
            associated with     the first time.
            advised to         Mr. Booth first came to see me on 12/08/08 complaining of
            advice on           shortness of breath which was worse when he was lying
            allergies           down. It was associated with tightness in the chest and
            allergic to         coughing.
            arrived at         She was advised to return the next day for a blood test and
            arrived in          follow‐up consultation. (verb)
                                For both children advice on recommended vaccines will be
                                 necessary. (noun)
                                She is not on any medication and has no known allergies.
                                Please note, the patient is allergic to penicillin.
                                The patient arrived at my surgery in a depressed state.
                                The family arrived in Australia in 2007.


   B      believe              I believe the patient needs urgent assessment and hospital
          borderline            admission.
                                She was noted to be overweight and has borderline
                                 hypertension.


   C        consistent with    I am writing to refer Mr. Walker, 40‐year‐old married
            commence            patient, presenting with signs and symptoms consistent with
            commence on         prostatic enlargement.
            confidence in      IV fluids were commenced in order to improve hydration.
                                Therefore, I commenced him on omeprazol 20 mg daily and
                                 strongly advised him to stop smoking cigarettes and stop
                                 drinking alcohol. (active)
                                She was commenced on 15 gram alepam 1 tablet nightly for
                                 her current anxiety and sleeplessness. (passive)
                                She lacks confidence in caring her baby in terms of breast
                                 feeding and bathing.


   D      discharge on         He will be discharged on the 12th of August.
          deteriorate          Since 28th of July her condition has deteriorated with

   deny               occasional disorientation.
            difficulty in     She denied vomiting and she was vague reporting about
            diagnosed with     laxatives.
            diagnosis of
                               Mr. Macintosh presented to me with the complaint of
                                difficulty in passing urine.
                               I am writing to refer my patient, Fletcher, a nine‐year‐old
                                Labrador cross dog who is diagnosed with high grade
                                lymphoma. (verb)
                               Histological results confirmed the diagnosis of high grade
                                lymphoma. (noun)


   E      evidence of         Examination findings revealed evidence of an enlarged
          enclosed             prostate.
                               I have enclosed the radiograph for your convenience.


   F      to follow           The patient was advised to follow a low fat diet.


  H       history             The patient first came to me yesterday evening with a one
                                day history of lower abdominal pain.
                               Mr. Abraham has a positive family history of prostate cancer.


   I      indicate            The family has indicated that they need an interpreter who
          indicative of        speaks Farsi or Arabic during follow‐up visits with this family.
          inconspicuous       However, there was slight swelling in the right groin
                                indicative of inguinal hernia.
                               His family and social history is inconspicuous.


   K      known               She is a known asthmatic since childhood and is on
                                Budesonide inhaler for the same.


  M       to make an          I have made an appointment for her through your
           appointment          receptionist.


  O       on examination      On examination, her blood pressure was 180/90 mm Hg with
          occasions            a regular pulse of 70 beats per minutes.

 Today she presented very anxious and depressed as she had
                                noted some blood in her motions on two separate occasions.


   P      provisional         Provisional diagnosis suggests prostate cancer.
          present at          Mr Gates presented at my clinic yesterday at 7 pm with a
          present to           complaint of lower back pain.
                               Today, he presented to me complaining of a regular dull
                                ache in the groin.


  Q       queries             If you have any further queries, please do not hesitate to
                                contact me.


   R      reveal              Examination today revealed a significantly increased right
          risk factors         groin swelling.
          a routine           His risk factors include: smoking 20 cigarettes per day, lack of
           recovery             exercise and a strong family history of hypertension.
          reluctant to        He has made a routine recovery and his wounds appear to
          rule out             be healing well.
          remarkable          He is reluctant to seek treatment.
           findings            I believe she needs an urgent assessment to rule out bipolar
                                disorder.
                               There were no other remarkable findings.


   S        suggestive of     Miss Jones is suffering from the signs and symptoms
            suspicious of      suggestive of ectopic pregnancy.
            suffering from    I am writing to refer this patient, a 60‐year‐old woman, with
            signs and          symptoms suspicious of bowel malignancy.
             symptoms          Ms. Taylor has been suffering from diabetes and she is
                                administering insulin injection by herself.
                               He is a 40‐year‐old man who is suffering from signs and
                                symptoms suggestive of peritonitis with perforated gastric
                                ulcer.


   T      treated with        He also has been suffering from hypertension which has
          tentative            been treated with Atenolol 50 mg daily.
                               My tentative diagnosis is dental fluorosis.



The Best in OET Training           www.firstacademy.in                           98 666 88 666
 
U         underlying          I would appreciate your assessment of this patient to find
            under control        out whether he has any underlying psychological problems.
            uneventful          Currently, her pain is under control with medication and she
            urgent               is tolerating fluids.
            unremarkable        Her second pregnancy and delivery were uneventful.
            to undergo          I would appreciate if you could give urgent attention to Mrs.
             treatment/surger     Woods’ problem.
             y/an operation      Cardiovascular examination was unremarkable and her
                                  electrocardiogram was normal.
                                 She underwent colonoscopy three years ago which was
                                  normal. (simple past)
                                 During hospitalization, the patient has undergone an
                                  electromyogram and X‐ray. (present perfect)


   V      vital signs           Her vital signs were normal, but she was overweight (85 kg).
                                  Therefore, she was advised to reduce weight and do
                                  exercise.


  W       with a complaint      Mr Gates presented at my clinic yesterday at 7 pm with a
           of                     complaint of lower back pain.

Prepositions

Prepositions of Time
In: ‘In’ is used for       On: ‘On’ is used for     At: ‘At’ is used for the
                                                                               Some words require
longer periods of          days and dates and       time of day and for
                                                                               no preposition
time                       some time expressions    some expressions
   In November               On Monday               At 6 o’clock              Yesterday
   In Spring                 On 20 November          At night                  Today
   In 2006                   On Christmas day        At lunch time             Tomorrow
   In the past               On his birthday         At that time              Last week
   In the future             On review               At the moment             This week
   In the morning            On examination          At the age of 45          Next week
   In the afternoon          On investigation        At birth
   In her childhood          On presentation
   In his twenties           On two occasions

Prepositions of Place
In: ‘In’ is used for inside of      On: ‘On’ is used for the        At: ‘At’ is used for a place of
something                           surface area of something       activity
   In Australia                     On the skin                      At home
   In hospital                      On the ground floor              At work
   In surgery                                                         At the wound site
   In the stomach                                                     At the clinic



                                         Common Errors
                       Incorrect                                        Correct
 His father died of cancer during the age of
                                                    His father died of cancer at the age of 50.
  50.
 In examination today, the patient was             On examination today, the patient was
  anxious and distressed.                            anxious and distressed.
 Initial examination on today revealed             Initial examination today revealed inflamed
  inflamed gums.                                     gums.
 On December 2006, the patient had his             In December 2006, the patient had his
  wisdom teeth removed.                              wisdom teeth removed.
 The patient’s family arrived at Australia in      The patient’s family arrived in Australia last
  last year.                                         year.
